newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels rule out killing any hostages.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels rule out killing any hostages.

text.p: Peruvian rebels holding 74 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on Wednesday said they did not plan to kill any of their captives.

"It is not in our minds to carry out executions, nor to give any ultimatums," a rebel spokesman, believed to be Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, said in a radio conversation monitored by Reuters.
"We have never spoken of executions," he added.
But the spokesman also said that with no tangible progress in negotiations, the crisis was "being pushed towards a military end."
He said the rebels in the residence were handling their captives with "a treatment respectful of their dignity." The hostages were all "in a controllable situation," he said.

Cerpa said gunshots from the compound were a response to threatening police manoeuvres outside including approaches to the residence. "The people detained know that," he said. "This forces us to take decisions in the heat of the moment."
